title: A recording can draw the pointer larger
body:
The pointer that `record` draws into its frames is `ARROW` in `decade/src/server/compositor/record.rs`: 17 rows of pixels, each drawn `scale` pixels square, where `scale` is the output's scale factor rounded. At scale 1 it is 17 pixels tall. In a 1749 × 1886 recording of a scratch pane, which GitHub shows at half size in a README, that is about 8 pixels on the page, too small to follow. coax's README recording ran into it on the first take driven by `scratch_input`.

## Proposal

- `record` takes an optional `pointer_scale`, the number of frame pixels each `ARROW` pixel takes, defaulting to the output's scale as now.

## Open

- Whether the arrow should be drawn from a larger source than 17 rows when scaled, so its edges stay smooth instead of blocky.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/3cd5690e
notes.text: The open point is settled with the simple choice. A scaled arrow is `ARROW` with each pixel repeated in a square of `pointer_scale` frame pixels, nearest-neighbour, so its edges stay blocky. No larger source was drawn. `pointer_scale` runs from 1 to 8, and decade refuses it with `pointer` false. Jack can revisit a smoother arrow if the blocky one looks wrong in a README.
